summary: A substantial intraday recovery reduces immediate downside risk, but technology still lags and semiconductor confirmation is missing.
bullish: QQQ recovered 2.74 percentage points from its morning observation; broad-market breadth improved.
AP reports roughly three quarters of S&P constituents advancing.
bearish: QQQ still trails SPY by 0.96 percentage points at 13:23 ET.
AI credit stress, tariff proposals and restrictive Fed expectations remain unresolved.

editorial.marketOverview: At 13:23 ET QQQ was down 1.64%, SPY down 0.68% and DIA up 0.29%. QQQ had been down 4.38% at 11:02 ET. AP separately reports broad participation improving, although technology remains a drag.
editorial.whatChanged: The recovery of 2.74 percentage points in QQQ and improved broad-market participation materially reduce the immediate downside scenario relative to the previous bearish assessment. No new curated event is evident from the unchanged count and newest event date.
editorial.marketInterpretation: The rebound is meaningful but not a confirmed AI leadership reversal. QQQ still lags SPY and the latest verified SOX observation is from late morning. Credit stress and tariff uncertainty remain relevant. No single catalyst for the bounce has been established.
editorial.threeDayPath: Wednesday shifts toward stabilization with downside risk. Friday may see follow-through or a renewed selloff in thin holiday liquidity. Monday depends on chip leadership, credit conditions and weekend oil developments.
editorial.bullCase: Holding the afternoon recovery into the close with improving chip participation could support a relief rally on Friday and Monday. Broad-market breadth is encouraging but not yet proof of Nasdaq breadth improvement.
editorial.bearCase: A failed rebound would expose the morning lows again, especially if semiconductor selling or AI financing stress resumes. Sticky inflation and proposed tariffs remain constraints.
editorial.watchNext: Verify Beige Book content, closing QQQ and SOX relative strength, VXN/VIX, paired yields, oil and Fed pricing. Friday early close and Sunday OPEC+ remain on watch; no new earnings catalyst independently verified.
